speech_03.transcript: I think these three things belong together. Put them over there, beside the other books, and then we can talk through the whole plan one step at a time.
speech_03.tail_transcript: the whole plan, one step at a time.

speech_01.transcript: Please bring my blue bag before we leave. Maybe we can buy some bread, make a simple meal, and meet Ben by the park before the bus comes back.
speech_01.tail_transcript: park before the bus comes back.

speech_02.transcript: Five friends visited the village on Friday. We found fresh flowers, shared a favorite meal, and enjoyed a very peaceful evening together before driving home through the soft fog.
speech_02.tail_transcript: together before driving home through the soft fog.

speech_04.transcript: Sarah says the streets are busy this morning. We can visit the stores, choose some supplies, and discuss our plans as we walk slowly past the square at noon.
speech_04.tail_transcript: slowly pass the square at noon.

speech_05.transcript: Shall we choose a jacket for James? We can measure the shelves, check the usual sizes, and share our decision before lunch today, then change it if you wish.
speech_05.tail_transcript: today then change it if you wish.

speech_06.transcript: Please sit here and tell me what you see. The green seats look different in this light, but the red desk is clear and the window seems a little brighter.
speech_06.tail_transcript: And the window seems a little brighter.

speech_09.transcript: Now is a good time to try another choice. I found a quiet house outside town and I would like to show you the garden and the old oak tree.
speech_09.tail_transcript: the garden and the old oak tree.

speech_07.transcript: My father left a black bag beside the cup. After lunch, we can walk past the shop and ask about the map together and then catch the last tram.
speech_07.tail_transcript: and then catch the last tram.

speech_08.transcript: You could choose the blue room with a good view. We can go home soon, cook some food and enjoy a quiet evening, then look at the moon.
speech_08.tail_transcript: evening, then look at the moon.

speech_10.transcript: We will walk along the river and look for the red building. When we arrive, Laura can tell us where the little room is and we will rest a while.
speech_10.tail_transcript: and we will rest a while.

speech_11.transcript: Thank you for joining me today. Tell me about your plans and we can work through the details together one step at a time until everything feels clear.

speech_12.transcript: Are you ready to begin? Take a moment. Then tell me what happened this morning and we can decide what to do next together without any hurry at all.
speech_12.tail_transcript: together without any hurry at all.

speech_25.transcript: Pack the paper box beside my backpack. Before Monday, bring the blue mug home and remind me to buy more milk, maybe some plums and a bit of butter.

speech_26.transcript: The ferry leaves after 5, so we have enough time. Find your gloves, fill the flask, and follow me down the path to the far end of the pier.
speech_26.tail_transcript: path to the far end of the pier.

speech_27.transcript: Please leave the envelope by the front window. Move the heavy basket carefully and give me a moment to finish my breakfast before we leave for the market.
speech_27.tail_transcript: breakfast before we leave for the market.

speech_28.transcript: Those thin curtains let the sunlight through. I think the room feels brighter now, and there is space for another small table, maybe with three chairs by the wall.
speech_28.tail_transcript: Maybe with three chairs by the wall.

speech_29.transcript: These oranges smell fresh and the lemons look nice. Choose six pieces for the guests, then place the rest beside the sink and rinse the glass bowls for later.
speech_29.tail_transcript: side the sink and rinse the glass bowls for later.

speech_30.transcript: The chef usually measures each portion before serving lunch. Choose a dish you enjoy and share your suggestion with the manager tomorrow at the usual meeting.

speech_31.transcript: The little bell rings when the green light appears. Keep the lid beside the shelf and let me see which piece fits, then we will lock the lid.
speech_31.tail_transcript: piece fits, then we will lock the lid.

speech_32.transcript: Sam left his hat on the counter after lunch. Our mother asked us to pack the cups and carry the basket upstairs and then sweep the back porch.
speech_32.tail_transcript: and then sweep the back porch.

speech_33.transcript: The soup should cool before you taste it. Put your spoon on the wooden tray and let the cook know how it tastes, whether it needs more salt or pepper.
speech_33.tail_transcript: whether it needs more salt or pepper.

speech_34.transcript: Enjoy the bright afternoon while the clouds are passing. I might ride my bike around the square and buy a small gift tonight for my oldest friend.

speech_35.transcript: We walked around the lake before the rain began. Riley remembered the narrow road and led us toward a warm little bakery nearby where we waited out the storm.
speech_35.tail_transcript: little bakery nearby, where we waited out the storm.

speech_36.transcript: Would you prefer coffee or tea? Either is fine. Let me know your choice and we can enjoy a few quiet minutes together before the others arrive.
speech_36.tail_transcript: minutes together before the others arrive.
